searchText: <pk910> I've created a storage spam scenario for spamoor and did some initial testing with it. It looks like we can fill ~2580 empty storage slots in a single block with a gas limit of 60M (can probably be optimized to do even more). Each value consumes 32B, and as it's stored in a key->value map, each key takes 32B too. So following that math, each of these storage spam blocks consumes 165kB additional storage (`2580*64`) Consuming 1GB storage takes ~6500 blocks, which is 21.6h only?? 🤔 That sounds a bit underpriced if we're worried about state growth.. <FunnyGiulio> well, doing this attack means you need to buy ethereum for 1 day <FunnyGiulio> I think it is very expensive actually <pk910> right :D this is worst case ofc, which needs a lot of eth to burn <FunnyGiulio> yeah imo worst case state growth does not really exist <FunnyGiulio> unless the attacker has an infinite money glitch ofc

<pk910> I've created a storage spam scenario for spamoor and did some initial testing with it.
It looks like we can fill ~2580 empty storage slots in a single block with a gas limit of 60M (can probably be optimized to do even more).
Each value consumes 32B, and as it's stored in a key->value map, each key takes 32B too.
So following that math, each of these storage spam blocks consumes 165kB additional storage (`2580*64`)
Consuming 1GB storage takes ~6500 blocks, which is 21.6h only?? 🤔 
That sounds a bit underpriced if we're worried about state growth..
